provenance: Telephone call, 2026-09-03, Larry's son asking the tier-1 questions from the interview guide and typing Larry's answers as he spoke them. The Camp Zama date question had been promoted to the head of the guide that morning. Raw capture: research/interviews/breakfast-questions.md, annotated in place under each question.
text: I don't know the Chaplains name. He wrote it down in a book.
researchNotes: The name is lost, but the second sentence is the useful half and was not asked for: the chaplain WROTE IT DOWN IN A BOOK. That is a contemporaneous written record of Larry reporting that he was alive while listed dead, made at Camp Zama in September 1965. Army chaplains kept activity logs and journals, and those are a records series. It is a thin thread - such logs are not reliably retained, and the hospital chaplain's office at Camp Zama may leave nothing - but it is the first indication that the misreport generated any paper at all outside the casualty list itself.
